article.plain_text:
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization across Constellation Energy’s nuclear fleet in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania. The modernization efforts will add nearly 1.1 gigawatts (GW) of electricity, strengthening the grid and lowering costs for millions of Americans across the PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) and Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) regions.
The loan advances President Trump’s Executive Order, Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base, which calls for DOE to facilitate 5 GW of power uprates from existing nuclear reactors. In March 2026, in accordance with the Executive Order, DOE launched its Utility Power Reactor Incremental Scaling Effort (UPRISE) to accelerate the expansion of the nation’s nuclear capacity by maximizing power generation from existing reactors. To date, 95% of President Trump’s 5-GW uprate and restart goal has been identified.
“The Energy Department is accelerating President Trump’s American nuclear renaissance and unlocking the full potential of our nation’s nuclear fleet,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “Uprates that maximize power generation from our existing nuclear facilities are yet another example of the commonsense energy addition policies the Trump Administration is embracing—ensuring more affordable, reliable, and secure energy for American families and businesses.”
The projects will add enough electricity to power more than 930,000 homes—lowering costs and strengthening grid reliability in Illinois, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and across the PJM and MISO regions. The investments will support more than 10,000 project-related jobs across Constellation’s nuclear fleet while delivering affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses.
“EDF is delivering on President Trump and Secretary Wright’s commitment to unleash American nuclear power by financing projects that modernize and expand our nation’s existing nuclear plants,” said EDF Director Gregory A. Beard. “These investments will add more reliable baseload power to the grid, help lower electricity costs, strengthen our nation’s energy security, and fuel long-term American prosperity.”
Constellation’s planned investments at Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle, and Quad Cities in Illinois; Calvert Cliffs in Maryland; and Limerick in Pennsylvania will produce more electricity from existing nuclear plants, maximizing America’s existing energy infrastructure while supporting growing demand for affordable, reliable, and secure power. EDF’s conditional loan commitment also includes an option to finance future uprate projects at additional Constellation facilities.
While this conditional commitment indicates DOE’s intent to provide a loan, Constellation must satisfy certain technical, legal, environmental, and financial conditions before the Department enters into definitive financing documents and funds the loan.

Up to 100% of men have microplastics in their semen

I got mine to zero. The first documented case.

A 2024 study detected microplastics in 100% of human and dog testicular tissue.

In another study, microplastics were detected in the semen and urine of all of 113 tested men from China.

Researchers broke down plastic type and how they affected sperm quality.

The most common came from packaging (polystyrene, polypropylene, and polyethylene).

PTFE, the synthetic polymer used in non-stick Teflon pans, proved the most lethal, creating 11% lower sperm concentration and 9% fewer total sperm.

Ten studies have measured microplastics in human semen. Five found 100% detection.

The rest from 84% down to 37%, but older tests used standard infrared microscopes that are blind to particles smaller than 10–20 microns. Newer studies used Raman spectroscopy, which can spot particles down to 1 micron.

So in short, 100% prevalence is plausible if not likely.

note_tweet.text:
In China, more than one in five workers is still employed in agriculture.

China makes and exports more goods than any other country. So, perhaps unsurprisingly, when we think about China’s economy, the first thing that comes to mind is often manufacturing — increasingly at the technological frontier in electric vehicles, batteries, and solar panels.

China’s position in manufacturing follows decades of economic transformation. The chart shows one aspect of this: the decline in agricultural employment.

At the turn of the 21st century, around half of all Chinese workers were employed in agriculture. One generation later, that share had more than halved, reaching 22% in 2025.

It's striking how far the share of workers in agriculture has fallen, and just as striking how high it remains. Agriculture employs more than a fifth of China’s workers, while accounting for less than 7% of its GDP.

(written by @EOrtizOspina)

After a breast cancer diagnosis, one of the hardest questions is whether it will come back.

@SimBioSys is helping doctors and patients better understand that risk. Powered by NVIDIA technology, its FDA-cleared TumorSight Risk analyzes an existing breast MRI alongside pathology and clinical information to estimate the risk of cancer returning at five and ten years.

For women with HR-positive, HER2-negative early-stage breast cancer, those insights can be available before surgery, giving them and their doctors more information as they talk through treatment options.

AI can help give patients and their doctors more information when the decisions ahead feel most difficult.

Tracking who trades with whom around the world.

The International Trade in Goods dataset from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) records how much each country exports to and imports from each of its trading partners. This data goes back to 1948.

Countries report to the IMF based on their own trade records and statistics. If this data isn’t enough, the IMF uses the country’s trading partners’ records instead.

This map shows, for each country in the world, the country from which it imported the most goods in 2025. For 83 of the 209 countries with data, that was China — this includes most of Asia, more than half of Africa, and most of South America. (Countries whose largest partner is not one of the most common ones are shown as “Other”.)

We recently updated eight of our charts with the IMF’s latest release, which adds data for 2025 for 209 countries and territories.

(This data update was led by @parriagadap.)

Energy Department Closes $5.1 Billion Loan to Lower Electricity Costs and Strengthen Grid Reliability in Iowa and Wisconsin
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) today announced the financial close of a $5.1 billion loan package to Alliant Energy to lower electricity costs, expand firm power generation, and strengthen grid reliability in Iowa and Wisconsin. The investments will add more than 2.6 gigawatts (GW) of new or upgraded power generation capacity and deliver more than $1 billion in electricity cost savings for American families and businesses across both states.
Today’s announcement advances President Trump’s Executive Order Strengthening the Reliability and Security of the United States Electric Grid by ensuring our nation has the dependable power needed to meet growing electricity demand and strengthen American energy security.
“The Energy Department is delivering on President Trump’s promise to lower electricity costs and unleash the full potential of American energy,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “These investments will drive down energy costs for families and businesses in Iowa and Wisconsin, strengthen our nation’s electric grid, and fuel American prosperity for decades to come.”
The projects will add enough electricity to power the equivalent of nearly 2 million homes—lowering costs and strengthening grid reliability in Iowa and Wisconsin. The investments will support new natural gas-fired power plants, energy storage systems, and upgrades to existing generation facilities, create hundreds of construction-related jobs, and deliver affordable, reliable energy for American families and businesses.
“Thanks to President Trump and Secretary Wright’s leadership, EDF is putting capital to work to expand America’s reliable energy infrastructure,” said EDF Director Gregory A. Beard. “By bringing new, dependable power online, we are strengthening our nation’s energy security and lowering electricity costs for families and businesses across Iowa and Wisconsin.”
This loan marks the Trump Administration’s tenth financial close, and the sixth and seventh utility financing completed through the Energy Dominance Financing Program.
Under President Trump’s leadership, EDF is financing American energy and manufacturing projects that meaningfully contribute to U.S. energy security, grid reliability, and lowering costs for all Americans, while more responsibly managing taxpayer dollars.

The Trump Administration's Project Uprise Is Accelerating America's Nuclear Renaissance Through Reactor Uprates, Restarts, and New Construction
THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION IS ACCELERATING AMERICA’S NUCLEAR RENAISSANCE
This week, Secretary Wright is visiting nuclear power plants in Illinois and Michigan to highlight the Trump Administration’s progress in expanding American nuclear power.
On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Secretary Wright is visiting Constellation Energy’s Byron Generating Station in Byron, Illinois, to announce the Energy Department’s conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization across the midwest and northeast.
On Thursday, October 29, Secretary Wright will also visit Michigan’s Palisades Nuclear Plant, where the Energy Department is supporting the historic restart of a previously shuttered nuclear facility—the first ever such restart in the United States.
The Energy Department's Utility Power Reactor Incremental Scaling Effort (UPRISE) is advancing President Trump's nuclear expansion agenda by supporting nuclear uprates at existing reactors, restarting closed plants, and building new reliable nuclear capacity.
With the addition of Constellation’s projects, UPRISE has identified approximately 4.7 gigawatts of additional nuclear capacity—95% of its 5GW goal by 2029. The Energy Department is supporting the majority of these investments through loan funding from the Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF).
Under President Trump’s leadership, the Energy Department is delivering on President Trump’s Executive Order, Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base, to expand American nuclear power and strengthen national energy security.
The executive order directs the Energy Department to work with industry to facilitate 5 GW of power uprates at existing nuclear reactors and begin construction of 10 new large reactors with complete designs by 2030.
The order also directs the Energy Department to prioritize financing activities that support nuclear plant restarts, reactor uprates, completion of stalled projects, advanced reactor construction, and the domestic nuclear fuel supply chain.
UNLEASHING NUCLEAR POWER THROUGH UPRATES, RESTARTS, AND NEW CONSTRUCTION
Through EDF, the Energy Department is directly investing in advancing nuclear uprates, plant restarts, and new construction to expand America’s reliable electricity supply.
The Energy Department is supporting commonsense investments in additional capacity at existing nuclear generating units –the fastest way to get new, reliable power online.
Constellation Energy (Adding nearly 1.1 GW): Nuclear uprates and modernization across Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania will add enough reliable electricity to power more than 930,000 homes, backed by an October 2026 conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion.
Vistra (Adding 433 MW; Preserving nearly 4 GW): Uprates and modernization in Pennsylvania and Ohio will add new generation capacity while preserving enough reliable power for more than 3 million homes. This was supported by an October 2026 conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion.
Vogtle Nuclear Uprates (Adding over 300 MW): Reactor uprates across 6 GW of existing nuclear capacity and license extensions for Hatch and Farley into the 2050s are expected to deliver more than $7 billion in electricity cost savings. In February 2026, the Energy Department closed a $26.5 billion loan package supporting these projects.
The Energy Department is supporting the historic restart of three previously shuttered commercial nuclear plants.
Palisades Nuclear Plant, Michigan (800 MW): The historic restart would return reliable nuclear power to Michigan’s grid and mark the first restart of a U.S. nuclear reactor that entered decommissioning status, supporting or retaining up to 650 high-quality jobs in Michigan, supported by a $1.5 billion loan to Holtec.
Crane Restart Project, Pennsylvania (835 MW): The restart would return enough reliable electricity to power approximately 800,000 homes and support more than 600 American jobs, backed by a $1 billion loan to Constellation.
Duane Arnold Energy Center, Iowa (615 MW): The restart would return enough reliable electricity to power nearly 500,000 homes, create approximately 1,500 construction and refurbishment jobs, and support more than 450 permanent operations jobs, backed by $1.9 billion in financing to NextEra.
The Energy Department is accelerating new nuclear construction to expand America’s reliable electricity supply.
The $17.5 billion American Nuclear Supply Chain Loans initiative is a conditional commitment that will help finance the equipment procurement for five eligible projects, with the goal of accelerating deployment of 10 new reactors by up to three years.

🚨 I HAVE NO MICROPLASTICS IN MY BALLS 🚨

This should not be possible.

Studies show that 100% of men have microplastics in their semen. I am the first human ever to show a complete reduction to zero.

This may be a world-first breakthrough in fertility research.

I had 165 microplastic particles in my semen just 18 months ago. Now, I have zero.

Five published studies have measured microplastics in human semen. Two found them in 100% of men. The other three found then in 44 to 76% of men tested, but those used methods that miss the smallest particles and the clear ones. Corrected for that, the real rate is likely 100%. Almost every man alive has plastic in his semen right now. The same applies to testicular tissue, testing 100% positive for microplastics.

Microplastics hurt sperm.

Human studies show the impact of various types of plastic, associated chemicals, and other toxins on male fertility:

+ 60% fewer normal shaped sperm (from PFAS)
+ 5x higher odds of low sperm count (from PTFE)
+ 10% lower sperm concentration (from PTFE)
+ 15% lower swimming ability (from PTFE)
+ 41% lower swimming ability (from PET)
+ 12% lower sperm swimming ability (from BPA)
+ 3x higher odds of low sperm count (from Phthalates)
+ 2x higher odds of poor swimming (from Phthalates)

The effects compound: each extra type of plastic drops sperm swimming ability by about 21%.

This matters even if you’re NOT trying to get pregnant.

Sperm count is one of the cleanest biomarkers of overall health we have. And microplastics don't stop at the testes.

The same particles are showing up everywhere we look. Studies show 4.5x higher rate of heart attack, stroke, and death in people with microplastics in their arterial plaque vs. those without. Microplastics were also found in 100% of human placentas tested.

100% of post-mortem human brains tested positive for microplastics. Brain concentrations rose ~50% between 2016 and 2024, and now sit at roughly 11x the levels found in the liver or kidney.

Where do these come from?
+ PTFE, commonly in non-stick pans
+ PET, water bottles
+ Phthalates, makes plastic soft and bendy
+ BPA, can linings
+ PFAS, stain-resistant fabrics & food packaging

Inside the body, plastic causes a kind of cellular rust. It triggers inflammation in the testicles, kills the cells that make sperm and drops testosterone. It's been confirmed across 39 animal and cell studies, then in human data.

MY PROTOCOL:

Note, what I did is n=1, not a controlled trial, I cannot prove cause.

1. Sauna (dry). My toxin blood panel confirms sauna clears plastic related chemicals: BPA, phthalates, PFAS, flame retardants, pesticides. 2. Reverse osmosis water filter. Drinking water is likely a major source of microplastic getting into your body. A reverse osmosis filter pushes water through a very tight membrane and strains the particles out. I filter everything I drink.

Trying to rid my environment of the big plastic items: cutting boards, cups, plates, food storage containers, non-stick pans, cling wrap, tea bags, water bottles, kitchen utensils, kettles, and synthetic clothing. Note, as hard as I try, I'm always finding new plastic things in my life. This can be all-consuming thing so try to just knock out the big ones.

I did all three interventions at the same time. I cannot say which one did the most work. What I can say is this: going from 165 to zero in 18 months is possible.

Jul 2025: 20 particles/mL
Apr 2026: 0 particles/mL
